record.title: [CSV Sniffer] `gzip` compressed, tab delimited file throws odd error
record.body:
### What happens?

When attempting to use `read_csv` to read in a gzip compressed, tab-delimited file, I get the error 

> Invalid Input Error: Error when sniffing file "/my/path/file.gzip". CSV options could not be auto-detected. Consider setting parser options manually.

This is unexpected because the file is parsed as expected (without proper column association) when any other delimiter is used. You can see that it's tab delimited, yet something about setting the delim option to `\t` breaks the ingest.

The issue appears to be with the column header.

Skipping another row and supplying my own columns works, but is undesirable.

### To Reproduce

Using the provided file, run `read_csv` without a specified delimiter or other conventional non-tab delimiter

```
from read_csv('test_apple_financial.csv.gz', compression='gzip', header=true, skip=3);
```

You'll see the columns and data, all in one column. It's possible to see the data and columns are tab-delimited.

Then run 

```
from read_csv('test_apple_financial.csv.gz', compression='gzip', header=true, skip=3, delim='\t');
```

This will prompt the error. 

The following will work but is undesirable

```
from read_csv('~/test_apple_financial.csv.gz', compression='gzip', skip=4, columns={
       'Transaction Date': 'varchar',
       'Settlement Date': 'varchar',
       'Apple Identifier': 'varchar',
       'SKU': 'varchar',
       'Title': 'varchar',
       'Developer Name': 'varchar',
       'Product Type Identifier': 'varchar',
       'Country of Sale': 'varchar',
       'Quantity': 'varchar',
       'Partner Share': 'varchar',
       'Extended Partner Share': 'varchar',
       'Partner Share Currency': 'varchar',
       'Customer Price': 'varchar',
       'Customer Currency': 'varchar',
       'Sale or Return': 'varchar',
       'Promo Code': 'varchar',
       'Order Type': 'varchar',
       'Region': 'varchar'
  });
```

[test_apple_financial.csv.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16273762/test_apple_financial.csv.gz)

record.title: [CSV Sniffer] Sniffer can now sniff files with extra delimiters
record.body:
This PR makes it possible that the sniffer can correctly sniff files with extra delimiters on the data part of the CSV file, if they don't have any data there.

For example
```
Vendor Name;Test
Start Date;06/02/2024
End Date;06/29/2024
Transaction Date;Settlement;Date
06/19/2024;06/22/2024;1435055555;		
06/14/2024;06/14/2024;1435055555;			
```
will result in a table with header:
```
Transaction Date;Settlement;Date
```

and data:
```
06/19/2024;06/22/2024;1435055555	
06/14/2024;06/14/2024;1435055555
```

Hence it will automatically skip the first 3 rows with an unfit number of columns, and it will ignore the extra delimiter on the data part of the file, after the header.

Fix: #13043

### Fixed

- Fixed a regression in 0.36.0 that broke Strict OOXML (ISO/IEC 29500)
  `_rels/.rels` links.

  [PR #681]: https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/681

- Fixed XLS string handling to preserve empty strings instead of discarding
  them. [PR #679].

  [PR #679]: https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/679

- Fixed XLSB workbook parsing to consume the body of unhandled workbook-global
  records. A leftover body was misread as the next record id, which either
  silently dropped the worksheet or panicked from an empty buffer. [PR #675].

  [PR #675]: https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/675

### What's Changed
* Add support for OOXML format by @saks in https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/681
* xls: preserve empty strings by @aquasync in https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/679
* fix(xlsb): consume unmatched workbook-global record bodies by @momomuchu in https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/675

record.title: Excel dates imported as java.util.Date, not OpenRefine date
record.body: **Describe the bug** Date columns from Excel files are imported as text into Refine. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Create a new project using an Excel file with dates in it, e.g. the one attached below. 2. The configuration screen for project creation will show the date column in black. Create the project anyway to try to convert it later on. 3. The date is read correctly from the Excel file (December 11th, 2018), but displayed in black, not green, i.e. not recognised as date. 3. Apply Common Transforms > To Date to the "Date" column. The date is still stored as text. See screenshot below. **Current Results** What results occured or were shown. **Expected behavior** A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen or to show. **Screenshots** **Desktop (please complete the following information):** - OS: macOS Mojave - Browser Version: Safari 12.02 - JRE or JDK Version: 1.8.0_181 **OpenRefine (please complete the following information):** - Version 3.1 [b90e413] **Datasets** Minimal file: [Date test.xlsx](https://github.com/OpenRefine/OpenRefine/files/2682052/Date.test.xlsx) **Additional context** This same file worked fine in Refine 2.8.
